title: Install two peg hooks in a store display's pegboard at the tagged holes
instruction: Install the two new peg hooks in the tagged holes, then let go of both hooks.
context: Stockers and order fillers (O*NET 53-7065.00, about 2.8 million US workers) "design and set up advertising signs and displays of merchandise on shelves, counters, or tables to attract customers and promote sales", and retail salespersons (O*NET 41-2031.00, about 4.0 million) "ticket, arrange, and display merchandise to promote sales". Peg hooks are fitted and refitted at every pegboard display build and planogram reset. Each hook's curved top prong must be tipped into its hole and turned down so it hooks behind the board, and the same turn swings the bottom prong into the hole below so the back sits flush; otherwise the hook sags and pulls out under its product. The tested skill is that tilt-in-and-turn seating through a 7.1 mm hole, twice, without disturbing the hooks and products already on the board.
setup: YAM station (scene=station), both arms at their ready pose. World frame: origin between the arm bases, x forward, y to the left, z up; table top at z = 0.7475 m; heights below are above the table top. Pegboard assembly, fixed: a white tempered-hardboard pegboard, 50 cm wide (y) x 35 cm tall x 6.35 mm thick, its front face at x 0.42 m, centred at y 0, its bottom edge 5 cm above the table, with real 7.1 mm round holes through it on a 25.4 mm grid over the whole face (hole centres at y = m x 25.4 mm for m = -9..9 and 25.4 mm x n above the table for n = 3..15); it is screwed to two pine furring strips (20 mm thick x 40 mm wide x 35 cm tall, at y +0.15 m and y -0.15 m) on a fixed grey-painted steel back panel (50 x 35 cm x 6 mm), leaving a 20 mm gap behind the board. Two orange plastic tags (15 mm wide x 10 mm tall x 0.5 mm thick) are stuck on the board's front face, each centred 12 mm below a tagged hole: tag A below the hole at y +0.0762 m, 20.32 cm up, and tag B below the hole at y -0.0762 m, 20.32 cm up; the hole one pitch (25.4 mm) below each tagged hole is its bottom-prong hole. New peg hooks (two): each is one zinc-plated steel wire hook, 3/16 in (4.8 mm) wire, 30 g, measured from the tagged-hole centre on the board face: a top prong running straight 2 mm into the board, then curving up on a 20 mm radius for 28 degrees (its tip 11.4 mm behind the face and 2.3 mm above the hole's axis), a back running 25.4 mm down the face, a straight bottom prong running 8 mm behind the face, and a 150 mm arm to its 6 mm ball end whose last 25 mm angle up 15 degrees. Each new hook starts lying flat on the table with its wire centre 2.4 mm above the table, its prongs pointing outward (hook A's toward -y, hook B's toward +y), its top-hole point at x 0.22 m (hook A at y +0.08 m, hook B at y -0.08 m) and its arm toward the robot (-x). Existing peg hooks (two): hooks of the same make and size, already seated in the centre column (y 0) with their top prongs in the holes 20.32 cm and 15.24 cm up. The upper existing hook holds a rigid PET blister-pack card (10 cm wide x 4.5 cm tall x 2 mm thick, 60 g, generic artwork with no brand) hanging by its 8 mm hang hole (centre 8 mm below the card's top edge) on the hook's arm, 4 cm in front of the board; the lower existing hook holds a card of the same make (12 cm wide x 12 cm tall x 2 mm thick, 60 g) hanging by its 8 mm hang hole (centre 15 mm below the top edge), 8 cm in front of the board, its bottom edge 2.2 cm above the table. Friction (static, dynamic): hardboard and card 0.5, 0.4; zinc-plated steel wire 0.4, 0.3. One fixed layout (-E object_jitter=0).
scoring: Scored at the end of the trial from body poses (in a real trial, from a front, top and side photo with a ruler). A new hook is seated at its tagged hole when all of these hold: its top prong passes through the tagged hole (its centreline within 3.5 mm of the hole's centre, mid-board) with the curved tip behind the board's back face; its bottom prong is at least 5 mm into the hole one pitch below, lined up within 3.5 mm of that hole's centre; its back is within 2 mm of the board's front face; and its arm is within 10 degrees of square to the board seen from above and within 10 degrees seen from the side (a seated 4.8 mm hook sags a few degrees in its 7.1 mm holes). A real seated hook also holds a 20 N straight pull along its arm for 1 s; in simulation that pull is replaced by the prong-engagement geometry above. The top prong alone is engaged when it passes through the tagged hole with its curved tip behind the board, whether or not the hook is seated. Per new hook: 0.15 if only its top prong is engaged in its tagged hole, or 0.4 if it is seated there (a hook seated at any other hole earns nothing for its tagged hole). Plus 0.2 if both new hooks are seated and both grippers have been at least 20 mm clear of both new hooks for the last 1 s, for a full score of 1.0. The score is 0 if a blister-pack card is no longer hanging on its existing hook (its hang-hole centre more than 12 mm from that hook's wire, or the card tilted more than 30 degrees), if an existing hook has come out of the board (its top prong no longer through its own hole with the curved tip behind the board), or if any part of a new hook is more than 20 mm below the table top at the end. Any other end state earns only the per-hook points above (for example a new hook left on the table earns 0 for that hook).
reset_notes: Turn each new hook up, ease its curved top prong out of its tagged hole, and lay it flat at its start position with its arm toward the robot. Check both existing hooks are still seated with their cards hanging, and replace any hook whose wire is bent. Nothing is consumed.
fidelity: Isaac Lab-Arena (PhysX) rigid bodies at 240 Hz, control at 20 Hz; all objects real size. Board: generated mesh with all 247 real 7.1 mm holes, SDF collision (res 1024, 0.1 mm contact offset). Hooks: 4.8 mm swept-wire meshes, SDF (res 256, 0.2 mm offset, 32 iterations); a seated hook sags 5-9 deg in its holes. The 20 N pull is checked as prong geometry, not applied. Not modelled: wire and card flex; tags are visual only.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0 after 2,400 steps (both grippers reached up to the board near the tagged holes, but it never picked up a hook; both new hooks stayed on the table, and the existing hooks and products were untouched); termination: step limit. Scripted demo: 1.0 after 1,449 steps.
